newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar loses recent gains, sluggish demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar loses recent gains, sluggish demand.

text.p: Indian sugar prices lost some of its recent gains on Wednesday with fresh consumer demand turning sluggish prompting light profit-taking, dealers said.
"Sugar arrivals from mills to the local market however remained low amid limited offerings by mill owners," a dealer said.

Ready delivery sugar S-30 slid by five rupees at 1,280/1,305 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved down by 6/10 rupees to 1,305/1,370 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery however remained steady at the improved level of 1,215/1,230 rupees per quintal on the back of continued buying by the bulk consumers at mill level.
"Bulk consumers remained active buyers following rising temperatures which may increase consumption of soft drinks in the coming days," one broker said.
Overall sentiment was steady at the close of the session.
Sugar ready delivery was up by 10/20 rupees per quintal on Tuesday.
